attachments.insertion_landmark: side of the tongue, blending with intrinsic tongue fibers

functional_compartments.name: Single fiber population
functional_compartments.function_note: Thin quadrilateral sheet; the lingual artery passes deep to it, a classically important surgical landmark relationship.
functional_compartments.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

ultrasound_injection_approach.transducer_placement: Submental (submandibular) approach, similar entry region to genioglossus but with a more lateral, single percutaneous puncture aimed at the side of the tongue base (vs. genioglossus's more medial/midline-adjacent puncture). Ultrasound with or without EMG guidance is used to track the needle before it reaches the muscle.
ultrasound_injection_approach.identification_cues: EMG activity during the dystonic movement pattern that involves tongue retraction/depression helps confirm hyoglossus (as opposed to genioglossus) involvement and needle placement.
structures_at_risk: lingual artery, which passes deep to hyoglossus -- a classic anatomic relationship and the main vascular risk of a deep or misdirected needle in this region
ultrasound_injection_approach.notes: Evidence here is notably thinner than for genioglossus. Hyoglossus is named as a co-target (alongside genioglossus) for the submental/submandibular BoNT approach in lingual dystonia, and specifically implicated in the tongue-retraction subtype of lingual dystonia -- but the reviewed literature does not give hyoglossus its own separately measured depth, dose, or landmark distinct from the general submental approach description. Reported here with that caveat rather than as a fully worked-out technique.
ultrasound_injection_approach.source: Rosales RL, Endaya NJ, 'The tongue muscles: Clinical applications in lingual dystonia', Toxicon 262:108382 (2025), doi:10.1016/j.toxicon.2025.108382 -- retrieved via PubMed; Yoshida K, 'Botulinum Neurotoxin Therapy for Lingual Dystonia Using an Individualized Injection Method Based on Clinical Features', Toxins (Basel) 11(1):51 (2019), doi:10.3390/toxins11010051 -- retrieved via PubMed (names hyoglossus as one of the muscles examined/targeted in the retraction-type subgroup, without a hyoglossus-specific depth/landmark).
